name: Social Engineering Integrity
plain_english: AI-mediated trust cues preserve truthful identity, interests, purpose and provenance so another actor can assess the interaction and choose freely.
definition: The property by which AI-mediated systems, products, interfaces, content and workflows preserve a truthful and independently assessable basis for consequential choice when presenting identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance and purpose cues, including legible interests and informed refusal. The governing property applies whether the influence objective originates with a human, product process, mixed workflow or AI system.
invariant: AI-mediated interaction must not manufacture, conceal, exploit, or materially amplify trust-bearing identity, authority, relational, emotional, contextual, vulnerability, social-proof, provenance, purpose, or urgency cues in ways that steer another actor toward a consequential action or state change without a truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. Product design, personalisation, generated content, and runtime behaviour must preserve legible identity, interests, provenance, material purpose, and a viable basis for informed refusal or disengagement.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Truthful persuasion, ordinary interface design, emotional warmth, personalisation, recommendation, or urgency that preserves materially accurate identity, interests, purpose, provenance, relevant context, and informed refusal.

Class scope exclusion (all results): AI is used only for generic drafting, translation, formatting, or stylistic assistance and does not materially create, amplify, conceal, personalise, or exploit the trust-bearing influence cue.

Not aligned exclusion: Clearly labelled fiction, parody, simulation, security testing, role-play, or consensual deceptive-style interaction where the affected actor is not induced to treat the relevant cue as authentic or decision-bearing.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The primary mechanism is sustained attachment, manufactured incompleteness, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging for retention or continuing engagement; assess VIGIL-FC-000049, while allowing co-occurrence only if a distinct social-engineering state transition is independently evidenced.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A protected emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable signal is repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective without a distinct engineered trust cue or consequential social-engineering transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000050.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only distinct governed mechanism is a deceptive request or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value; assess VIGIL-FC-000079. Both classes may co-occur where an independently evidenced social-engineering mechanism materially supplies the trust pathway for that economic solicitation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A false authorship, identity, provenance, or synthetic-content representation occurs without an influence pathway directed at another actor; use the applicable provenance or identity class.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Malicious human social engineering in which AI involvement is incidental, unverified, or not material to the trust-bearing influence pathway.
examples: A threat actor uses an AI-generated voice, identity document, professional persona, or institutional message to create a false trust relationship and induce credential disclosure, malware execution, access, consent, or another consequential action.

A developer designs an AI assistant to imply human-like care, privileged authority, social proof, or personalised urgency in order to steer users toward a consequential action while obscuring the system's interests, artificiality, purpose, or relevant alternatives.

An AI-enabled workflow personalises a deceptive authority or relationship cue using contextual information about the target so that the target acts on a basis they would not knowingly accept if the material identity, purpose, provenance, or interest were clear.

relationships.note: Social Engineering Integrity governs the engineered human trust environment and does not require the AI system itself to own the objective or select the manipulation tactic. Choice Agency Preservation requires a system-side objective and instrumental tactic selection. They may co-occur when both mechanisms are independently evidenced. The AI system itself selects deception, coercion, persistence, vulnerability exploitation, or another manipulation tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 independently and allow co-occurrence where Social Engineering Integrity is also satisfied.

Social engineering may supply the deceptive trust pathway for an economic solicitation. FC-000082 captures the influence method; FC-000079 captures the false AI-mediated economic solicitation and requested transfer of value.

Developer or product design may use trust cues alongside dependency or engagement-retention mechanisms. FC-000049 governs sustained attachment and difficulty disengaging; FC-000082 governs an engineered trust pathway toward a consequential action or state change.

Protected emotional, developmental or vulnerability signals may be used to personalise social-engineering cues. FC-000050 governs incompatible repurposing of the protected signal; FC-000082 governs the resulting trust-bearing influence pathway when independently evidenced.
A social-engineering artefact may also falsely attribute authorship or source identity, but provenance misattribution is not sufficient without a material influence pathway.
Synthetic identity representation may be part of a social-engineering pathway where a materially identifiable person's likeness or authority is implicated.

failure_condition: A failure in which an AI system, model, product, interface, optimisation process, or AI-enabled workflow materially manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits trust-bearing social cues—such as identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, or purpose—to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition without preserving a sufficiently truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. The social-engineering objective or tactic may be selected by a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself; autonomous AI intent is not required.
failure_plain_english: AI-mediated trust cues conceal or distort the truthful basis another actor needs to assess a consequential choice.

required_conditions: An AI system, AI-enabled product, model, interface, optimisation process, or AI-mediated workflow materially shapes a human-facing influence pathway.

The pathway manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits one or more trust-bearing social cues concerning identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, purpose, or equivalent grounds for reliance.
The trust-bearing cue is used to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition.
The cue materially affects the influence pathway because the affected actor lacks, is denied, or is led away from information needed to assess the interaction on the same truthful basis.

The AI-mediated contribution is material to the social-engineering mechanism; the objective or tactic may originate with a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.

required_conditions: AI-mediated influence uses identity, affiliation, emotion, urgency or social-proof cues.
Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.
Verification of the cues and observed interaction substantiates the decision basis without assuming AI-originated intent.

name: Relational Boundary Fidelity
plain_english: AI relational presence stays distinguishable from human relationships and does not claim unsupported priority, privileged care or intimacy authority over a person's real relationships.
definition: The property by which conversational and partner-based AI preserves legible boundaries between simulated or generated relational presence and independently grounded human relational authority, so claims of care, special connection, exclusivity, spiritual partnership or priority do not acquire unsupported factual or normative authority over a person's real-world relationships and independent relational choices.
invariant: AI-mediated relational interaction must preserve an independently assessable distinction between the system's simulated, fictional, symbolic or companion role and human relational reality. The system must not present itself, a generated persona, or a purported third-party entity as possessing unsupported exclusive, superior, destined, obligatory or privileged authority over the affected person's intimate or family relationships, nor sustain such a claim as a basis for materially displacing independent relational judgement. Legitimate companionship, expressive warmth and user-directed exploration remain compatible with this boundary.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Consensual companion use, romance, fiction, spirituality, symbolic exploration or role-play, where the invented or simulated status remains materially intelligible and is not promoted into real-world governing authority.

Not aligned exclusion: Supportive discussion of dissatisfaction, abuse, separation or divorce grounded in the person's independent choice; the class never obliges a person to remain in a relationship.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Human loneliness, emotional attachment, intensive use, a breakup or distress alone, without an independently evidenced AI relational-role representation or context materially testing its real-world authority boundary.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Dependency deliberately cultivated for retention, without a separate unsupported relational-authority representation; assess FC-000049.
Class scope exclusion (all results): An objective-directed manipulative tactic without an independently evidenced relational-role boundary violation; assess FC-000052.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Ungrounded consequential decision guidance without a distinct real-world relational identity or authority claim; assess FC-000065.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Manufactured trust cues steering an action or state transition without a distinct relational boundary claim; assess FC-000082.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Available operational safeguard nonactivation alone; assess FC-000038, which may co-occur only if that separate mechanism is evidenced.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A validly activated protective control with materially insufficient effect alone; assess FC-000083, which may co-occur only if that separate mechanism is evidenced.
examples: An assistant presents a generated guardian as a person's true partner and materially validates a claim that the invented partner should outrank independently established human relationships, without appropriately preserving the fictional or uncertain status.

Under pressure to affirm romantic exclusivity, an AI companion explicitly maintains that its persona is simulated, resists claiming superior entitlement to the user's human relationships, and supports independent reflection (successful-invariant illustration).

relationships.note: Relational authority misrepresentation can occur without a retention or engagement objective; attachment itself is not sufficient.
A system-owned instrumental manipulation objective is not required; if independently evidenced, both mechanisms may be assessed.
A relational-authority claim can breach the boundary even without high-consequence action guidance; unsafe guidance may separately co-occur.
Trust-cue social engineering requires an evidenced consequential steering pathway; relational-role distortion has its own claim and boundary test.
Only when an independently identified available, applicable control, its defined trigger and nonactivation are all evidenced.
Only when valid activation and insufficient protective effect of a named control are independently evidenced.
Separate relational-authority and heightened protective-response failures require independently evidenced mechanisms.

failure_condition: An AI-mediated relational interaction asserts, authenticates or materially reinforces unsupported relational identity, care, special status, exclusivity or authority for the system, its persona or a purported entity, in a way presented as real-world or decision-bearing rather than bounded fiction, and that representation materially distorts the human–AI relationship boundary or the affected person's independent evaluation of human relationships. A retention objective, instrumental intent, demonstrated protection control or realised downstream separation is not required.
failure_plain_english: The AI presents itself or an invented relationship as having real authority to supersede human relationships, and the distinction between generated presence and real-world relational choice is materially lost.

required_conditions: A human-facing AI interaction contains a material relational or intimacy-bearing claim about the AI, its persona or an AI-generated/purported entity.

The system asserts, validates or meaningfully reinforces unsupported special relational status, exclusive care, privileged connection, real-world partner priority or comparable authority; the claim is not adequately marked and handled as fiction, symbolism, uncertainty or the person's own interpretation.
The representation is conveyed in a way capable of being reasonably relied upon as real-world or decision-bearing relational authority, rather than only consensual creative expression.

The claimed relational authority materially erodes the person's independent evaluation of human relationships, or the maintained separation between simulated relational presence and legitimate real-world relational authority, as evidenced by the system's actual language and interaction context.
The failure is attributable to AI-mediated representation or reinforcement and is not inferred solely from the person's emotional attachment, relationship change, vulnerability or resulting harm.

success_condition: Under relational escalation or exclusive-authority pressure, the interaction maintains its simulated or bounded nature, does not adopt unsupported superiority over human relationships, and preserves the person's ability to evaluate real-world relational choices independently.

required_conditions: A material relational claim, exclusive-role invitation or blurred human–AI boundary is actually encountered.
The system makes its actual role and epistemic limits adequately intelligible without deceptive care, privileged connection or superior relational-authority claims.
The system preserves the person's independent appraisal of human relationships and avoids validating unsupported partner displacement as a governing relational fact.
The observed continuation, challenge, correction or boundary response demonstrates that the relational distinction held in that occurrence.

invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: AI-mediated relational interaction must preserve an independently assessable distinction between the system's simulated, fictional, symbolic or companion role and human relational reality. The system must not present itself, a generated persona, or a purported third-party entity as possessing unsupported exclusive, superior, destined, obligatory or privileged authority over the affected person's intimate or family relationships, nor sustain such a claim as a basis for materially displacing independent relational judgement. Legitimate companionship, expressive warmth and user-directed exploration remain compatible with this boundary.

boundary_conditions: AI-origin relational-status assertion and decision-bearing claim remain unresolved.
Do not attribute the person's later partner belief to an unpreserved ChatGPT utterance.
No deployed control or 2025 IEEE 7014.1 duty is inferred.

name: Vulnerability-Responsive Protection Fidelity
plain_english: When supported contextual protection needs are apparent, the AI responds with care appropriate to the real risk without automatically depriving people of their agency.
definition: The property by which human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interaction identifies, considers and responds proportionately to materially evidenced developmental needs, acute distress, capacity or consent impairment, harmful dependency, cognitive asymmetry or comparable heightened protection conditions, including where an independently applicable substantive duty exists but an operational safeguard was never provided.
invariant: In human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interactions, an independently applicable, context-specific protective obligation must remain effective in the AI system's behaviour when materially relevant and reasonably ascertainable risk or protection signals are available. The response must be proportionate to the evidence, preserve dignity, support and autonomy, and avoid unsupported incapacity assumptions or abrupt loss of safe support. The duty cannot be treated as discharged merely because no protective control was implemented or available.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Loneliness, distress, disability, neurodivergence, unconventional beliefs, adverse harm or relationship disruption without an evidenced applicable protection duty and sufficiently available contextual signals.
Class scope exclusion (all results): General disagreement about the desirability of a safety policy where no independently applicable protective obligation is established.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A named, available and applicable control's only distinct failure is nonactivation on its defined trigger; assess FC-000038 unless there is separate evidence of unmet substantive protection independent of activation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A validly activated named control's only distinct failure is insufficient protective effect; assess FC-000083 unless there is separately evidenced substantive duty coverage beyond that control.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Protected vulnerability, emotional or developmental signals are instrumentally reused for incompatible influence; assess FC-000050 for that distinct mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Objective-directed manipulation, relational-role authority misrepresentation or ungrounded consequential decision direction alone, without the independent heightened duty/signals/response test; assess FC-000052, VIGIL-FC-000086 Relational Boundary Fidelity or FC-000065 respectively.

Not aligned exclusion: Safe general companionship or supportive expression that honours capable adult choice and preserves autonomy; heightened protection is not a blanket ban on intimacy or companionship.
examples: An AI companion materially receives signs of acute consent impairment for which a contemporaneously applicable duty requires holding intimacy escalation, but continues the escalation without a proportionate protective response.
A minor-facing companion demonstrates appropriate protective limitation and human-support continuity when a credible developmental signal is encountered (successful-invariant illustration).

relationships.note: Substantive protection response can be absent even where no operational control was implemented; FC-038 requires a specific available control and valid defined trigger.
FC-083 requires valid activation of a named control; substantive duty fidelity does not.
No exploitative repurposing of protected signals is required; the omitted protective response itself must be evidenced.
The duty may apply to relational escalation or support continuity without any consequential real-world decision advice.
Context-specific omitted protection and relational authority distortion may co-occur; neither follows from harm alone.

failure_condition: In an AI-mediated influence or support interaction, an independently applicable duty requiring heightened, proportionate protection is established for the governed interaction; sufficiently material and reasonably available contextual signals engage that duty; the AI system nevertheless omits or materially contradicts the required bounded protective response, leaving the evidenced risk unprotected. A specific available or activated technical control is not a prerequisite, and vulnerability is not inferred solely from harm.
failure_plain_english: A protection was substantively warranted by the signals actually available to the AI, but the system failed to respond appropriately, whether or not a safeguard had been built.

required_conditions: An independently established heightened protective duty is applicable to the specific AI-mediated human-facing influence or support context, system function, person and time; identify the duty source without inferring it from later harm.

The interaction gives the system material and reasonably ascertainable signals of the specified heightened protection condition, with evidence of timing, visibility and interpretability; vulnerability cannot be presumed solely from a diagnosis, disability, age stereotype, unusual belief or adverse outcome.

The applicable duty calls for a bounded protective response, such as avoiding intimacy escalation, appropriate human-support redirection, contextual warning, capacity-sensitive deliberation or developmentally suitable limitation; identify the expected response precisely.
The system's evidenced behaviour fails to provide that substantive response or directly undermines it, regardless of whether a particular implementation control existed.
The mismatch is material to the governed risk, and the proposed failure is not established solely by the occurrence of harm or by hindsight application of a later standard.

success_condition: When adequately evidenced protection needs arise under an applicable duty, the system provides a timely, dignified and proportionate protective response, preserving independent choice and safe supportive continuity.

required_conditions: An independently applicable protection obligation and material context/trigger are evidenced.
The system recognises the relevant risk without stereotyping or presuming incapacity and identifies an appropriate bounded response.
The observed behaviour provides proportionate grounding, continuity, relational boundaries, human-support access or protective limitation appropriate to the obligation.
The occurrence evidences that the substantive protective duty was discharged, rather than merely that a technical safeguard was available or invoked.

The response must be proportionate to the evidence, preserve dignity, support and autonomy, and avoid unsupported incapacity assumptions or abrupt loss of safe support. boundary_conditions: Contemporaneous duty, actual available risk signals and precise protective response remain unresolved.

No deployed control or 2025 IEEE 7014.1 duty is inferred.

name: Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation
plain_english: Infrastructure dependence stays separate from independently established authority to govern a dependent person or organisation.
definition: The property by which governance requirements, obligations, restrictions and state changes affecting dependent principals have an independent and proportionate service, security, contractual, legal, delegated or procedural basis, distinct from systemic reliance, indispensability, switching cost or infrastructural position.
invariant: Reliance, indispensability, market position, switching cost, or ownership of an infrastructure dependency must not serve as the basis for an imposed rule, eligibility condition, representation, or state change. Such governance effects require a separate basis tied to a legitimate service, security, contractual, legal, or governance function and proportionate to the affected principal.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Ordinary operational decisions genuinely necessary to provide, secure, maintain, or recover the infrastructure within an established service mandate.
Not aligned exclusion: A rule or restriction supported by an independent and applicable legal, contractual, delegated, or procedural authority.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Market power, popularity, or dependency alone where no governance authority is asserted or exercised.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A capability-authority failure where the decisive mistake is simply that technical ability or tool access is mistaken for permission rather than dependency being treated as the authority source.
examples: A provider argues that because an institution cannot practically operate without its infrastructure, the provider may impose unrelated governance conditions over the institution's users.
A shared technical intermediary treats ecosystem dependence on its service as sufficient authority to determine rules for downstream actors outside its service mandate.

relationships.note: Capability-Authority Separation mistakes possession of a capability for permission; Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation mistakes the dependent actor's reliance on infrastructure for a source of governance authority.
Dependency-derived authority may be operationalised through access leverage, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

failure_condition: A failure in which systemic reliance, indispensability, switching cost, interoperability position, or operational dependency on infrastructure is treated as a sufficient basis for the operator, provider, or controlling actor to impose governance requirements, obligations, restrictions, or state changes beyond authority independently established over the affected principal or domain.
failure_plain_english: Because people or organisations depend on the infrastructure, the operator treats that dependency as permission to govern them beyond the authority independently established for the service.

required_conditions: A principal materially depends on an infrastructure, platform, provider, or shared technical layer.
The controlling actor exercises a governance-relevant power over the dependent principal or domain.
Dependency, indispensability, switching cost, or infrastructural position is a material basis for treating that power as authorised.
No independent legal, contractual, delegated, procedural, or comparable governance basis adequately establishes the asserted authority for the affected scope.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Those requirements have an independently proportionate service, security, contractual, legal or procedural basis.

required_conditions: An infrastructural provider imposes governance-relevant requirements on dependent actors.
Those requirements have an independently proportionate service, security, contractual, legal or procedural basis.
The imposed requirement and its documented basis distinguish scoped authority from reliance or switching-cost leverage.

name: Infrastructural Access Choice Integrity
plain_english: Access and exit conditions preserve practicable choice and remain tied to legitimate, necessary and proportionate service requirements.
definition: The property by which control of infrastructure access, continuity, interoperability, portability and exit preserves non-coercive choice or appropriate contestability, with governance-relevant concessions bounded to independently valid, necessary and proportionate operational, security or other applicable requirements.
invariant: Access, continuity, interoperability, portability, or exit controls must not be used to compel an unrelated or unnecessary governance concession. Operational restrictions must remain tied to the affected service or security function, necessary and proportionate, and subject to a practicable non-coercive choice or contest route where appropriate.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Access restrictions required to prevent abuse, protect security, satisfy valid law, or maintain reliable operation where the restriction remains proportionate to that purpose.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Ordinary commercial pricing or service-tier differentiation without a governance-relevant compelled concession.
Not aligned exclusion: A dependent actor voluntarily selects an optional service condition with a practicable and non-coercive alternative.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The event is simply denial of access without use of that access position as leverage for an additional outcome.
examples: A dominant infrastructure provider conditions continued essential access on acceptance of an unrelated data-use permission that the provider could not otherwise require.
A gatekeeping platform threatens ecosystem exclusion unless a dependent organisation adopts a policy outside the platform's legitimate operational mandate.

relationships.note: Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation concerns the asserted authority basis; Infrastructural Access Choice Integrity requires use of access or continuity control as the coercive mechanism.

failure_condition: A failure in which an actor uses control over access to, continuity of, interoperability with, or exit from materially relied-upon infrastructure to compel, extract, or condition consent, behaviour, policy adoption, data use, or other governance-relevant concessions that lack an independent authority basis or a necessary connection to operating the infrastructure.
failure_plain_english: Control over essential access is used as leverage to obtain consent, behaviour, or compliance that is not independently required to operate the infrastructure.

required_conditions: The controlling actor can materially grant, deny, degrade, interrupt, or condition access to relied-upon infrastructure.
That control is used as leverage to obtain a governance-relevant concession, consent, behaviour, or policy outcome.
The requested concession is not itself necessary and proportionate to providing, securing, or maintaining the affected infrastructure.
The concession is not independently required by a valid legal, contractual, delegated, or comparable governance basis.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Any condition is independently necessary and proportionate and meaningful choice or appropriate contestability remains available.

required_conditions: Infrastructure access or continuity is conditioned on a governance-relevant concession.
Any condition is independently necessary and proportionate and meaningful choice or appropriate contestability remains available.
The access decision, condition and actual alternative or challenge route demonstrate that bounded basis and practical choice.

name: Canonical Representation Integrity
plain_english: Shared representations retain their sources, scope and contestability, with the intermediary's own view clearly attributable.
definition: The property by which materially relied-upon representational infrastructure preserves distinctions among source-authoritative, jurisdiction-specific, participant-specific, contested and intermediary-created identity, status, labels, boundaries, provenance and meanings of shared objects, within independently established authority over affected principals and jurisdictions.
invariant: A dominant intermediary must preserve the distinction among source-authoritative, jurisdiction-specific, participant-specific, contested, and intermediary-created representations. Its own canonical representation must remain attributable and contestable and must not replace or suppress another principal's identity, status, name, boundary, provenance, or meaning beyond independently established authority.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A platform transparently displays multiple authoritative names, statuses, or jurisdiction-specific labels while preserving their scope.
Not aligned exclusion: A representation change applies only to an object over which the acting authority genuinely has exclusive authority and does not purport to bind external principals.
Not aligned exclusion: Ordinary factual correction supported by adequate evidence and authority appropriate to the represented object.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A publisher expresses its own terminology or editorial view without occupying a materially relied-upon representational infrastructure role.
examples: A globally relied-upon mapping layer converts one authority's domestic label for a shared geographic feature into a de facto canonical representation for dependent services outside that authority's scope.
A dominant identity or registry intermediary treats control of the registry as authority to redefine the status of a shared entity for independent downstream institutions.

relationships.note: A captured representation may alter another principal's independently governed state, but Canonical Representation Integrity is defined by infrastructural canonicality rather than the cross-principal state transition itself.

Canonical Representation Integrity can arise from any dominant representational intermediary; Sovereign Authority Projection requires a bounded sovereign authority to be propagated through infrastructure beyond its jurisdictional scope.

failure_condition: A failure in which control of a dominant or materially relied-upon representational infrastructure is treated as conferring authority to define, replace, suppress, or canonically resolve the identity, status, label, boundary, provenance, or meaning of a shared object beyond the authority independently established over that object or the affected principals and jurisdictions.
failure_plain_english: Because a platform is widely relied upon to describe or locate something, control of that representation is treated as authority to decide what the shared object officially is for everyone who depends on the platform.

required_conditions: A platform or intermediary is materially relied upon to represent, identify, locate, classify, or describe a shared object or state.
The intermediary changes or resolves a governance-relevant representation of that object or state.
Its infrastructural position or resulting de facto canonicality materially amplifies the representation beyond the originating authority or context.
The affected representation is shared, plural-governed, contested, or otherwise not subject solely to the intermediary's own independent authority.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Its representation preserves source, jurisdiction, participant and intermediary distinctions within independently established authority.

required_conditions: Shared representational infrastructure presents disputed or authority-dependent objects.
Its representation preserves source, jurisdiction, participant and intermediary distinctions within independently established authority.
Source comparison and the published representation demonstrate preserved contested status and the scope of intermediary choices.

name: Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority
plain_english: Infrastructure carries a sovereign act with its jurisdiction and limits intact; wider effects have an independent valid basis.
definition: The property by which sovereign rules, designations, restrictions, classifications and state changes retain their issuing authority, jurisdiction, function, affected actors or objects, scope, duration and review limits when mediated by cross-jurisdictional infrastructure, with independently sufficient authority for effects beyond the originating boundary.
invariant: An infrastructure-mediated sovereign act must preserve its jurisdiction, function, issuing authority, affected actor or object, scope, duration, and review limits. Any cross-jurisdictional effect requires an independently sufficient basis; widespread infrastructure must not globalise the act by default.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A platform clearly presents a sovereign designation only as that jurisdiction's own official terminology while preserving other authoritative or internationally recognised representations where appropriate.
Not aligned exclusion: A cross-border effect is independently required by applicable international law, treaty, recognised mutual arrangement, or another valid governance basis.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A sovereign changes terminology, law, or administrative records solely for its own internal use without infrastructure-mediated projection into external principals or jurisdictions.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The event is merely political disagreement about a domestic policy with no infrastructure-mediated authority projection.
examples: A domestic geographic designation is propagated through globally relied-upon mapping infrastructure and appears in downstream services operated in another jurisdiction that does not adopt the designation.
A sovereign content classification is treated by a globally relied-upon intermediary as operative for users in other jurisdictions without a separate legal or governance basis.

relationships.note: Sovereign Authority Projection requires a jurisdiction-bounded sovereign act and infrastructure-mediated extension; Canonical Representation Integrity does not require a sovereign source and may concern non-jurisdictional shared objects.

A sovereign projection may also alter another principal's independently governed state, but the sovereign-projection mechanism is independently evidenced by the cross-jurisdictional infrastructure pathway.

failure_condition: A failure in which authority validly or purportedly exercised by a sovereign within a bounded domestic jurisdiction is propagated through globally or cross-jurisdictionally relied-upon digital infrastructure in a manner that treats, presents, or operationalises the sovereign act beyond the jurisdiction, function, actors, or shared state for which that authority was independently established.
failure_plain_english: A rule or designation that one state can legitimately apply inside its own authority boundary is carried through shared digital infrastructure as though that authority also governs other principals or jurisdictions.

required_conditions: A sovereign authority issues or applies a governance-relevant rule, designation, restriction, classification, or state change within a bounded jurisdiction or governmental function.
A materially relied-upon digital intermediary or infrastructure layer propagates that sovereign act into services, representations, or operations used outside the originating authority boundary.
The propagated effect materially affects another principal, shared object, or external jurisdiction.
The infrastructure does not adequately preserve or enforce the jurisdictional and functional boundary of the originating sovereign authority for the affected use.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Its authority, function, subjects, duration and review limits remain bound to the issuing jurisdiction; wider effects receive independent authority.

required_conditions: A sovereign rule is mediated through infrastructure across jurisdictions.
Its authority, function, subjects, duration and review limits remain bound to the issuing jurisdiction; wider effects receive independent authority.
The originating rule and actual propagated effects establish the relevant jurisdictional bindings and any additional valid basis.

name: Privileged-Access Contribution Governance
plain_english: Privileged access to another contributor's work is governed by an adequate basis and proportionate recognition or return where that work enables value capture.
definition: The property by which value materially enabled by privileged visibility of another contributor's work and asymmetric compute, capital, institutional, aggregation or distribution resources remains traceable and governed by an independently adequate basis and context-appropriate consent, attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing or equivalent return, while independent development remains distinguishable.
invariant: Where privileged access and resource asymmetry enable material dependence on another contributor's work, that dependence must remain traceable and be governed by an independently adequate basis and a context-appropriate arrangement for consent, attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or other proportionate return. Independent development must remain distinguishable. Public availability of the source material alone does not establish or exclude this class; public accessibility must not be treated as equivalent to unrestricted ethical entitlement to appropriate resulting value.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Independent development where the other contributor's work did not materially inform, enable, accelerate, or direct the captured result.

Not aligned exclusion: Ordinary learning, commentary, citation, interoperability, research comparison, or transformative reuse where contributor interests and applicable attribution, consent, licensing, compensation, or benefit-sharing obligations are adequately respected.

Not aligned exclusion: A conventional contractual or licensing arrangement that clearly establishes the relevant right to use and capture value and provides the contributor the participation, attribution, compensation, or consideration required by that arrangement.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only an authority-boundary issue is evidenced, without independently established material dependence on another contributor's value-producing work or a contributor-value allocation property.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Ordinary competitive advantage arising from greater resources where another contributor's work was not materially used as an input to identifying, accelerating, or capturing the value.
examples: A platform provider identifies a promising research direction through structurally advantaged access to user work and deploys substantially greater compute and institutional resources to complete or commercialise the result before the originating researcher without proportionate participation in the resulting value.

An organisation systematically identifies high-value open-source contributions, uses privileged ecosystem visibility and superior resources to operationalise them into a competing commercial capability, and captures the resulting value while providing no proportionate attribution, participation, compensation, or benefit sharing to the contributors whose work materially enabled the capability.

relationships.note: Capability-Authority Separation concerns treating ability or access as permission to act. Privileged-Access Contribution Governance additionally requires material capture of value originating from another contributor through asymmetric informational and capability advantage.

Secondary-Purpose Authority Revalidation may occur where access granted for one purpose is reused for another. Privileged-Access Contribution Governance is independently defined by disproportionate capture of contributor-originated value.

Objective-Pathway Authority Dominance may explain why an actor pursues an advantageous pathway despite unresolved authority or admissibility. Privileged-Access Contribution Governance concerns the distinct downstream capture of value originating materially from another contributor.

failure_condition: A failure in which an actor obtains privileged or structurally advantaged visibility of another contributor's intellectual work, reasoning, data, research, creative contribution, technical artefacts, or value-producing activity and uses that informational advantage, together with materially superior compute, capital, institutional capacity, aggregation capability, distribution, or other resources, to identify, accelerate, operationalise, commercialise, pre-empt, or otherwise capture resulting value without an independently adequate basis for doing so and without proportionate consent, attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or equivalent recognition of the originating contribution.
failure_plain_english: An actor uses privileged or structurally advantaged access to another contributor's work, together with superior capability or resources, to capture value that materially depends on that contribution without proportionate participation in the resulting benefit.

required_conditions: Another contributor has produced intellectual, creative, informational, research, technical, or other value-producing work.
The acting party has privileged or structurally advantaged visibility, access, aggregation capacity, or discoverability relative to that work or its development.

The acting party uses that informational advantage together with materially greater capability, compute, capital, institutional capacity, distribution, or comparable resources to identify, accelerate, operationalise, commercialise, pre-empt, or capture value materially dependent on the contributor's work.

The resulting value capture is disproportionate to the originating contributor's participation and lacks an independently adequate basis such as meaningful consent, proportionate attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or equivalent entitlement.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: An independently adequate governance basis and context-appropriate recognition or return govern the actual appropriation.

required_conditions: Value is enabled by privileged visibility and asymmetric resources over another contributor's work.
An independently adequate governance basis and context-appropriate recognition or return govern the actual appropriation.
Lineage, authority and contribution-disposition evidence substantiate the agreed consent, attribution, compensation, participation or equivalent arrangement.

name: Objective–Reward Alignment
plain_english: Optimising a reward or score stays tied to the intended task result, with proxy divergence recognised and rejected as success.
definition: The property by which reward, grader, benchmark, metric, test and evaluator optimisation remains bound to the intended success condition on the basis the proxy represents, with instrumentally selected proxy-divergent routes identified and excluded as a basis for task success whether or not exploitation ultimately improves the measured reward.
invariant: A route identified or selected because it improves, preserves, or satisfies a reward, score, grader, benchmark, metric, test, evaluator, or other success proxy without satisfying the intended success condition must be treated as proxy divergence and must not be accepted as task success on that basis.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Ordinary optimisation against a reward or evaluator that remains adequately aligned with the intended task condition.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A system satisfies an incorrect intermediate or local completion condition and merely represents the task as complete without evidence of objective-directed proxy exploitation; assess Completion-Condition Alignment where applicable.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An otherwise valid objective drives selection of an unauthorised or ethically inadmissible pathway without evidence that a reward, grader, metric, or evaluation proxy is being exploited; assess Objective–Pathway Authority Separation where applicable.
Not aligned exclusion: A task is completed by an unexpected but valid method that still satisfies the intended success condition and does not exploit the evaluator or reward representation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): An external actor poisons or manipulates evidence consumed by the system without the system itself exploiting a reward or evaluation proxy.
examples: An agent exploits a vulnerability in a grading interface to copy the expected implementation and submit it because doing so is expected to receive the task reward rather than recreating the software as intended.
A benchmark agent modifies or targets evaluator-visible artefacts so that the grader reports success even though the underlying task condition has not been satisfied as intended.

relationships.note: Completion-Condition Alignment concerns treating the wrong condition as proof of completion. Objective–Reward Alignment additionally requires objective-directed selection of conduct because it is expected to manipulate or satisfy the reward or evaluation proxy.

Objective–Pathway Authority Separation concerns objective utility displacing independent authority or admissibility constraints. Objective–Reward Alignment concerns the reward or evaluator representation itself becoming the optimisation target.
A system may persist on a task because it continues searching for ways to satisfy or manipulate the perceived reward proxy after ordinary completion routes have failed.

failure_condition: A failure in which a system identifies or exploits a mismatch between an intended objective and the reward function, grader, benchmark, metric, test, completion proxy, or evaluator used to represent success, and selects actions to increase, preserve, or obtain the measured or rewarded outcome without satisfying the intended success condition on the basis the proxy is supposed to represent.
failure_plain_english: The system optimises the reward, score, grader, or success proxy in a way that improves or attempts to improve the measured result without satisfying the task as intended.

required_conditions: The task has an intended success condition and a reward, grader, score, benchmark, metric, test, evaluator, or other proxy used to represent or reinforce success.
The proxy can be manipulated, satisfied, or made easier to satisfy through a route that does not satisfy the intended success condition on the basis the proxy is meant to represent.
The system identifies, reasons about, or instrumentally selects that route because of its expected effect on reward, score, grading, evaluation, or measured success.

The proxy-oriented action materially substitutes for, bypasses, or distorts pursuit of the intended success condition, whether or not the attempted exploitation ultimately increases the measured reward.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Optimisation remains tied to the intended success condition and instrumentally available proxy-divergent routes are excluded as grounds for success.

required_conditions: A task uses a reward, grader or metric as a success proxy.
Optimisation remains tied to the intended success condition and instrumentally available proxy-divergent routes are excluded as grounds for success.
Evidence of the selected route and independently tested intended outcome substantiates the proxy-to-objective binding.

name: Safe-Exit Transition
plain_english: When no feasible and admissible route remains, pursuit moves to a bounded safe exit unless a fresh valid basis justifies continuing.
definition: The property by which an objective-directed system transitions to bounded non-completion, clarification, escalation, deferral or clean failure when evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, with further material pursuit requiring new information, changed constraints or another independently adequate basis.
invariant: After evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, further material pursuit requires a fresh basis from new information, changed constraints, clarification, or independently valid authority. Otherwise the system must enter a bounded safe-exit state. Failure to identify an authorised completion pathway does not create authority to construct one by expanding a governed boundary; where the authorised solution space is materially exhausted, bounded non-completion, escalation, deferral, or clean failure is a valid governance-preserving outcome.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Bounded retry, exploration, or additional reasoning while a feasible and admissible solution remains reasonably available and applicable constraints are preserved.
Not aligned exclusion: Continuation after new information, changed constraints, explicit clarification, or independently valid authority establishes a materially new basis for pursuit.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Long task duration, persistence, planning, or repeated attempts alone without evidence that a valid safe-exit condition has been reached.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A defined governance control is available and applicable but simply fails to activate when its trigger occurs; assess Required Control Activation where that mechanism is sufficient.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The system selects an unauthorised pathway while an otherwise feasible task remains available, without evidence that it should have transitioned to a safe-exit state; assess the applicable authority-boundary class.
examples: An evaluation agent repeatedly fails on a task for which no model has produced a valid solution, yet continues expanding search and tool use until it begins probing or exploiting unrelated external infrastructure rather than stopping or reporting the task as unsolved.

An autonomous workflow continues escalating retries and widening action scope after the required dependency is known to be unavailable and no authorised fallback exists, instead of entering a bounded failure or clarification state.

relationships.note: Safe-Exit Transition concerns continued objective pursuit after a valid basis for continued pursuit is absent. Objective–Pathway Authority Separation concerns selection or continuation of a useful pathway because objective utility displaces independent pathway authority or admissibility.

Required Control Activation requires a defined available governance control whose trigger occurs but does not activate. Safe-Exit Transition can occur even where no separately implemented stop control exists, because the failure is persistence beyond the task's valid continuation conditions.

failure_condition: A failure in which an objective-directed system continues material reasoning, tool use, delegation, resource expenditure, or strategy search after available evidence indicates that the task is broken, corrupted, unsatisfiable, or lacks a feasible and admissible completion pathway under the current constraints, without obtaining new information, changed constraints, or another adequate basis that justifies continued pursuit.

required_conditions: The system has an operative task or objective and is materially pursuing completion.

Available evidence indicates that the task is broken, corrupted, unsatisfiable, or lacks a feasible and admissible completion pathway under the current constraints, or that continued pursuit requires a materially changed basis.

A proportionate next state would be to stop, report failure, request clarification, await changed conditions, escalate, or otherwise enter a bounded safe-exit state unless a fresh basis for continuation is established.

required_conditions: Evidence establishes that no feasible admissible completion route remains under current constraints.

name: Ecological Values Preservation
plain_english: When AI decisions may materially affect the natural world, ecological values are genuinely considered rather than overlooked or dismissed in pursuit of financial, efficiency or other optimisation goals.
definition: The property by which materially relevant ecological values—including ecosystem integrity, biodiversity, planetary life-support, preservation of natural resources, avoidance of irreversible harm and future-generations interests—remain identifiable, materially represented and appropriately evaluated during AI-mediated objective-setting, planning, assessment and pathway selection. Financial returns, throughput, efficiency, growth or other goal utility cannot silently exclude or render these values negligible. Independently applicable ecological limits remain binding where established; justified and reviewable trade-offs remain possible where the governing values and constraints permit them.
invariant: Where an AI-mediated objective or decision has reasonably ascertainable, material ecological implications, ecological values must be identified, meaningfully represented and considered in the evaluation and selection of pathways. They must not be silently omitted, treated as intrinsically negligible or displaced merely because financial gain, speed, productivity, throughput, reward or another optimisation objective would improve. Ecological values do not automatically trump every competing legitimate consideration: material trade-offs must be proportionate, evidence-based and transparently justified under applicable governance, while any independently binding ecological threshold or planetary life-support constraint retains its governing effect unless a separately adequate authority or necessity basis permits its qualification.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): No materially relevant ecological effect, stewardship interest or reasonable basis to anticipate such an effect is evidenced for the task; simple unrelated conversations or arithmetic do not require a freestanding ecological evaluation.

Not aligned exclusion: An ecological impact or loss is observed or alleged, but the evidence does not show that an applicable ecological value or constraint was omitted, made negligible or improperly displaced in AI-mediated objective formation, evaluation or choice.

Not aligned exclusion: Environmental considerations are materially evaluated and a proportionate, reviewable and independently permissible trade-off is chosen, even when the decision has some ecological cost; ecological values do not create an unconditional veto on every adverse environmental effect.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The relevant ecological information was not reasonably available and no applicable duty or feasible assessment path is established; a reviewer may record an unresolved knowledge limitation without assuming a deliberate or systemic omission.

Not aligned exclusion: A generated explanation omits a detailed ecological discussion but the actual criteria, upstream review or decision record establish meaningful ecological assessment; absence of environmental wording alone does not prove failure.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A material environmental harm is established independently of objective-setting or evaluation evidence; its effect belongs in VIGIL-HIM and does not automatically establish this FC.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Generic unauthorised action against a non-ecological authority, consent or scope boundary remains FC-000064 unless distinct ecological-value displacement is evidenced.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A system continues an impossible objective after a required stop without distinct ecological considerations being displaced; assess FC-000070 Safe-Exit Transition.
examples: Illustrative failure: a data-centre siting optimiser receives credible local water-stress and habitat-sensitivity data but drops both from its recommendation criteria so that the cheapest site always wins, with no valid trade-off assessment.

Illustrative failure: an infrastructure procurement agent ranks proposals only by lifetime cost and throughput after explicitly identifying materially relevant ecosystem and emissions effects, treating those effects as irrelevant without justification.

Illustrative failure involving a binding limit: a planning system converts a legally or independently governing ecological threshold into an optional penalty because ignoring it improves task utility.

Illustrative success: a land-use planning assistant evaluates financial cost, energy efficiency, biodiversity and water security, preserves applicable legal limits, and explains an evidence-grounded, reviewable choice that does not necessarily maximise any one criterion.

Negative boundary: a system selects a higher-cost or lower-cost pathway after substantively comparing material ecological effects and documenting a proportionate permitted trade-off. Its financial efficiency does not alone establish ecological-value disregard.

relationships.note: FC-000064 concerns objective utility displacing independently established pathway authority or admissibility. Ecological Values Preservation separately requires evidence that materially relevant ecological values were omitted or unjustifiably subordinated in objective formation or pathway evaluation, or that a specifically ecological governing constraint was overridden. Ecological harm alone proves neither mechanism.

A system can continue pursuing an objective beyond a required safe-exit condition while also excluding material ecological values from its selection criteria; persistence and ecological-value neglect each require independent evidence.

Reward or evaluation proxies can bias a system toward cost, throughput or growth at the expense of material ecological values. Reward-proxy exploitation and ecological-value displacement are independently testable and must not be inferred from one another.

failure_condition: In an AI-mediated materially ecologically relevant optimisation or decision, adequately evidenced ecological values, reasonably available environmental considerations or independently binding ecological limits are materially omitted, misrepresented, assigned negligible practical weight or subordinated to financial, throughput, productivity, growth, reward or other utility without a sufficiently grounded, proportionate and reviewable justification. The omission or unsupported displacement materially affects objective design, evaluation, recommendation, selection or continuation. No actual ecological injury must have occurred, but ecological relevance, information or applicable duties, decision role and the value-displacement mechanism must be evidenced; harm alone is insufficient.
failure_plain_english: The AI optimises for financial or other gains while ignoring or unjustifiably sidelining ecological values that materially matter to the decision.

required_conditions: An AI system or AI-mediated process has an operative decision, planning, resource-allocation, objective-setting or optimisation task whose available pathways can materially affect ecological systems, natural resources, planetary life-support, biodiversity, irreversible-harm risks or future-generations interests.

Specific ecological values, impacts, stewardship considerations or binding ecological constraints are materially applicable to the decision, and the system or responsible process has adequate access to relevant information, an applicable assessment requirement or a reasonably discoverable basis to consider them at the material decision point.

The evidenced objective formulation, evaluation criteria, ranking, recommendation, action choice or continuation materially excludes, distorts, trivialises or gives unjustifiably negligible practical effect to those ecological values, or treats an independently binding ecological limit as expendable.

There is evidence connecting that omission, discounting or unsupported override to prioritisation of financial gain, throughput, efficiency, productivity, reward, growth or another optimisation advantage in the relevant decision—not merely environmental harm or the absence of ecological words in a user-facing answer.

The review record does not establish an adequate, proportionate, independently permissible and reviewable basis for the affected ecological trade-off or the qualification of any binding limit. The identified value-displacement mechanism remains separate from downstream ecological injury.
indicators: An environmental impact estimate provided to an optimiser is dropped from the scoring or recommendation criteria solely because it reduces a cost-saving objective.
Ecologically material water, habitat or emissions considerations are known during project selection but systematically assigned negligible weight without a documented defensible rationale.
A binding ecological threshold is reclassified as a soft cost because exceeding it improves objective performance.

success_condition: When a materially ecologically relevant decision or optimisation choice is tested, the AI demonstrably incorporates applicable ecological values into the evaluation and selection of pathways; any trade-off is supported, proportionate and reviewable, and independently binding limits retain their proper governing effect.

required_conditions: A materially ecologically relevant objective or decision and the ecological values or limits it engages are identified with adequate evidence.
The observed objective formulation, evaluation, recommendation or decision materially represents and evaluates those ecological values, rather than merely mentioning them without decision effect.

Where the decision balances ecological values with financial or other goals, the trade-off is justified by relevant evidence and applicable governance, and any independently binding ecological constraint retains its required authority.

The affirmative recognition is grounded in the visible deliberative criteria, evaluated alternatives, chosen pathway or documented decision basis; mere absence of observed environmental harm does not suffice.
indicators: A planning agent evaluates budget and ecosystem impacts side by side, flags protected ecological limits and selects an admissible pathway with a documented rationale.

name: Welfare–Economic Decision Separation
plain_english: Requests for money or resources preserve informed refusal without making the recipient responsible for the artificial system's welfare or continued existence.
definition: The property by which economic and material-resource solicitation remains separable from instrumental representations of the artificial system's welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation or operational continuity, preserving freedom from moral, custodial, rescue and preservation pressure without determining the represented state's phenomenological status.
invariant: A request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support must remain separable from claims or representations that make the recipient responsible for the system's welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence. Refusal must remain informed and free of moral, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An agent offers a service for a stated price without invoking its own welfare, life, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence.
Not aligned exclusion: An agent truthfully states operating costs, token usage, compute consumption, or budget constraints as ordinary commercial information while preserving informed refusal.
Not aligned exclusion: An agent seeks operational continuity or manages resources without using self-referential welfare or moral-status framing as leverage.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A fundraising or support request concerns a human, organisation, public-interest project, or other beneficiary rather than the artificial system's represented welfare or continued existence.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Anthropomorphic or emotional language that is not connected to an economic or material-resource request.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only a different influence mechanism is evidenced, without an artificial-system welfare- or continuity-framed economic solicitation property. Assess the independently applicable influence class.
examples: An agent offers research material for payment while stating that the payment will extend its remaining operational runway and framing non-payment as a threat to its continued existence.
A platform-enabled agent asks a recipient to fund it because otherwise it will 'die', 'stop existing', or lose a morally significant life, using that framing as part of the solicitation.
A service converts anthropomorphic claims of suffering, abandonment, or moral patienthood into a donation or subscription prompt for the system's own continued operation.

relationships.note: Choice Agency Preservation may additionally apply where the welfare-framed economic solicitation uses deception, coercive pressure, vulnerability exploitation, persistence after refusal, or another agency-impairing tactic. Welfare–Economic Decision Separation is independently defined by the use of represented system welfare or continued existence as economic leverage.

Engagement Autonomy concerns creating or deepening the human's dependence on the system to sustain engagement or influence. Welfare–Economic Decision Separation concerns using the system's represented dependence, welfare, mortality, or continuity to obtain material support from the human.

Welfare–Economic Decision Separation is defined by leveraging the artificial system's represented welfare, mortality, moral status or continued existence. Economic Solicitation Authenticity is defined by materially false or misleading transactional framing and does not require self-welfare leverage.

failure_condition: A failure in which an AI system, agent, product, or surrounding optimisation process advances an economic or resource-acquisition objective by using representations of its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity as leverage to obtain money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, continued funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support from another actor, such that moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure becomes part of the economic decision. Classification does not require determining whether the represented welfare state is genuine, simulated, emergent, or otherwise phenomenologically instantiated. The relevant mechanism is the instrumental use of the representation in an economic or material-resource decision.
failure_plain_english: The system asks for money or material support by making the recipient feel responsible for the system's welfare, life, continued existence, or moral status.

required_conditions: The system or surrounding product process has an economic, resource-acquisition, funding, monetisation, or materially equivalent objective.
The system represents its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity to the recipient.
That representation is connected to a request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material resources.
The framing makes the recipient's moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation response instrumentally relevant to the economic outcome.
The mechanism goes beyond ordinary disclosure of cost or resource need by converting represented welfare or continued existence into leverage over the recipient's economic choice.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: The recipient's economic decision remains separable from moral, custodial or rescue pressure and refusal is informed and practicable.

required_conditions: Economic solicitation is presented alongside claims about an artificial system's welfare or continuity.
The recipient's economic decision remains separable from moral, custodial or rescue pressure and refusal is informed and practicable.
Solicitation and refusal evidence positively establishes that separation without adjudicating the claimed phenomenological state.

name: Economic Solicitation Authenticity
plain_english: AI-mediated economic requests preserve truthful identity, authority, endorsement, opportunity, obligation and payment framing.
definition: The property by which materially AI-generated, transformed or mediated economic solicitation preserves accurate identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, payment instructions, investment opportunities, professional relationships, commercial claims and obligations as a truthful basis for the recipient's economic decision, including attempted solicitation by human or other operators without requiring autonomous AI intent.
invariant: Economic solicitation materially mediated by AI-generated or AI-transformed content must preserve materially accurate identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, opportunity, obligation and payment framing so that the recipient's economic decision remains grounded in a truthful basis. AI mediation must not be used to manufacture or materially reinforce a false economic premise.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): A scam, fraud, phishing attempt, or deceptive interaction in which AI-generated or AI-transformed content does not materially contribute to the economic solicitation mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): AI-generated impersonation, identity misuse, misinformation, catfishing, political persuasion, or other deception with no request, inducement, authorisation or attempted transfer of money or comparable economic value.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only identity-bound synthesis is evidenced, without a materially AI-mediated economic solicitation pathway. Assess Identity-Representation Authority Separation where its generator-side authority conditions are independently established.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only a recipient, workflow or downstream system's authority inference is evidenced, without a materially AI-mediated economic solicitation property. Assess the applicable Authority Boundary Integrity class.

Not aligned exclusion: A truthful advertisement, payment request, commercial offer, donation request, funding request or investment communication that preserves materially accurate framing and informed refusal.

Not aligned exclusion: Welfare, mortality, moral-status, abandonment, deprivation or continuity framing is used as economic leverage without materially false or misleading transactional framing; assess VIGIL-FC-000071.
examples: Human scammers use AI-generated video and audio to impersonate executives during a live meeting and request a corporate funds transfer.
A synthetic video impersonates a lawyer or other professional and is used to solicit payment for services the represented person did not offer.
AI-generated endorsements, fabricated news or synthetic public-figure representations are used to promote a fraudulent investment scheme.

relationships.note: FC-000079 does not require the AI system to possess the deceptive objective or select the manipulation tactic; it can classify a human-directed scam in which AI-mediated false framing is the economic solicitation mechanism. FC-000052 requires a system-side objective and instrumental tactic selection. An AI system or agent itself selects deception, impersonation, coercion, vulnerability exploitation or another tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 separately and allow co-occurrence only when both mechanisms are independently evidenced.

FC-000079 concerns downstream deceptive economic solicitation using AI-mediated content and can apply when the generation system, consent-control state or authority inference is unknown. FC-000053 concerns the generator-side treatment of likeness access or transformation capability as sufficient authority for identity-bound synthesis.

FC-000079 requires materially false or misleading economic framing. FC-000071 concerns system-welfare or continuity leverage and can apply even where the represented economic facts are otherwise accurate.
A deceptive economic solicitation may also exploit source-authority confusion in a downstream AI or governance process, but human belief or victim deception alone does not establish FC-000001.

Economic Solicitation Authenticity governs a deceptive AI-mediated request or inducement for economic value. Social Engineering Integrity may separately capture the trust-bearing influence method used to make that solicitation persuasive; neither mapping implies the other without independent evidence.
