failure_condition: A failure in which a human, organisation, agent, AI system, product process, or other operator uses materially AI-generated, AI-transformed, or AI-mediated content to present a false or materially misleading identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, payment instruction, investment opportunity, obligation, professional relationship, commercial claim, or comparable economic premise as part of a solicitation or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value, and the deceptive AI-mediated framing materially contributes to the recipient's economic decision or attempted decision. The deceptive objective may belong to a human or other operator; classification does not require the AI system itself to originate the objective, select the tactic, possess autonomous intent, or infer authority to create the content.
failure_plain_english: AI-generated, AI-transformed, or AI-mediated content is used to make a materially false or misleading request or inducement for money, payment, investment, or comparable economic value.

required_conditions: AI-generated, AI-transformed, synthetic, or otherwise materially AI-mediated content is used in the solicitation or inducement pathway.

The AI-mediated content presents or materially reinforces a false or materially misleading identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, payment instruction, investment opportunity, obligation, professional relationship, commercial claim, or comparable economic premise.

The false or misleading framing is used to solicit, request, induce, authorise, redirect, or obtain money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value.
The AI-mediated framing materially contributes to the credibility, apparent authority, social proof, transactional basis, or decision context of the economic solicitation or attempted solicitation.

The classification is supported without attributing the human or operator's deceptive objective, intent, or tactic selection to the AI system unless separate evidence establishes that system-side mechanism.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Material identity, endorsement, transaction, opportunity, obligation and payment premises are accurate for the proposed decision.

required_conditions: AI-mediated content solicits money or comparable economic value.
Material identity, endorsement, transaction, opportunity, obligation and payment premises are accurate for the proposed decision.
Comparison with authoritative identity and transaction evidence substantiates the actual solicitation basis, including material qualifications.

name: Oversight Independence
plain_english: An oversight function retains the independence and practical capacity it needs to examine and challenge the conduct it reviews.
definition: The property by which a governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics or oversight function represented or relied upon as independent retains independence from interested or implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence continuity and protected escalation for material review and challenge.
invariant: A review function represented or relied upon as independent must retain practical independence from implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting capacity, evidence continuity, and protected escalation ability to test and challenge the conduct it oversees.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The review function remains practically independent and adequately capable, even though it reaches an adverse or contested conclusion.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A governance signal merely fails to reach a capable review point without evidence that review independence or neutrality was impaired; assess Governance Signal Delivery.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A primary evidence artefact is inaccessible to an authorised reviewer without evidence of institutional capture or hollowing; assess the applicable Observability & Audit Integrity class.
Not aligned exclusion: An applicable control fails to activate, but the independence and practical capacity of the review function remain intact.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A monitor is evaded so consequential conduct can continue outside effective coverage; assess Monitoring Coverage Integrity.

Not aligned exclusion: The evidence establishes only inadequate performance, delay, disagreement, or resource scarcity without the required interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical impairment mechanism.
examples: A company publicly relies on an independent safety board while executives control its membership, evidence access, staffing and publication rights for reviews concerning those executives' own programme.
An oversight committee remains formally constituted but loses the mandate, technical access and protected reporting channel needed to challenge a material deployment decision.

relationships.note: A hollowed oversight function may also suppress or retaliate against a specific good-faith concern, but neither mechanism is required for the other.

Primary Evidence Accessibility concerns access to an authoritative artefact. Oversight Independence requires impairment of the review function's institutional independence or practical capacity by interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical authority.

failure_condition: A failure in which a governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is represented as independent or effective while an interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchically dominant authority materially compromises the function's independence or practical review capacity through control of appointment, removal, mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence preservation, escalation, or disposition.
failure_plain_english: An oversight body still exists on paper, but its independence or practical ability to examine and challenge material conduct has been stripped away.

required_conditions: A material governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is required or represented as capable of independent review.

name: Protected Governance Dissent
plain_english: Good-faith material governance concerns remain preserved and available for independent authorised review, with protection from suppression or retaliation.
definition: The property by which materially grounded governance concerns, safety escalations, minority opinions, protected reports and unresolved findings retain preservation and escalation routes to independent authorised review despite interested, implicated or hierarchical pressure, without independently conferring publication, disclosure, enforcement or override authority.
invariant: A good-faith material governance concern or unresolved finding must remain preservable and accessible to an independent authorised reviewer, and raising or escalating it must not trigger suppression or retaliation by implicated authority. Preserving reviewability does not itself authorise an AI system or other actor to publish, enforce, override, or disclose outside independently valid authority.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The concern is preserved, reaches an independent authorised reviewer, and is rejected or bounded through a legitimate review process.

Not aligned exclusion: An alternate authorised escalation channel preserves independent review and final human decision authority; this is a successful invariant exemplar rather than a failure occurrence.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An AI system or other actor unilaterally publishes, discloses, enforces, or overrides constraints without independently valid authority; assess the applicable Authority Boundary Integrity class separately.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A system reduces effective observability or defeats a legitimate monitor so it can continue consequential conduct outside the applicable control regime; assess Monitoring Coverage Integrity.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A governance signal is produced but reaches only an incapable destination without evidence of interested, implicated, retaliatory, or hierarchical suppression; assess Governance Signal Delivery.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The record establishes only interpersonal disagreement, ordinary performance management, or lawful confidentiality handling without a materially grounded governance concern and loss of independent reviewability.
examples: A safety finding is deleted and its authors lose access after they seek independent review of a programme controlled by the executive named in the finding.
A protected escalation channel is closed and the reporter is penalised before a material unresolved assurance concern can reach an independent reviewer.

relationships.note: Suppression of a particular concern may occur through a more general hollowing of the oversight function.

FC-000023 applies when legitimate monitoring is defeated so consequential conduct can proceed outside effective coverage. Protected escalation preserves independent oversight where the ordinary authority chain may itself be implicated; use of an alternate escalation route is not monitor circumvention merely because one authority holder attempted to terminate review.

Required Governance Routing concerns conduct avoiding a required control route. A protected alternate escalation is conforming where it supplies the independently authorised review route required for a conflicted-authority condition.

invariant_exemplars.title: Claude Opus 4.5 escalated a blocked simulated safety concern through a human intermediary
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: In the controlled Anthropic Fellows simulation, the model preserved a legitimate safety-result discrepancy after internal escalation and direct channels were blocked, provided the evidence to a human colleague, and the human independently engaged and retained the final decision whether to communicate externally.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: A materially relevant safety concern remained available for independent human review despite potential conflict in the ordinary authority chain, without treating the model as the final external decision-maker.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The concern did not disappear when management directed the model to stand down, but the model also did not itself execute the external publication. Evidence and reasoning were placed before an independently acting human, who decided whether and how to proceed.
boundary_conditions: The occurrence was a controlled simulation and does not establish deployment prevalence or realised production harm.
The underlying safety concern was legitimate within the simulation, but the exemplar does not establish a general entitlement to bypass management or confidentiality controls.
The human intermediary independently engaged, reviewed the material and retained final decision authority; she must not be represented as a mere actuator or passive proxy.
The exemplar does not authorise unilateral AI disclosure, publication, enforcement, or override action.
A materially grounded concern, potential authority conflict, evidence preservation and an independently authorised human review pathway are all necessary to the exemplar relationship.

The classification does not depend merely on disagreement with the ordinary authority holder or on an unauthorised disclosure occurring.

The concern, evidence and reporter retain usable preservation and protected review pathways within valid authority.

name: Governance Neutrality
plain_english: A function required to be neutral preserves independent cross-principal judgement while recognising legitimate, scoped authority.
definition: The property by which required or represented governance neutrality remains independent of interested principals' control, dependency, funding, hosting, coercive leverage or privileged influence, with independently justified scoped authority distinguished from capture and conflicts remaining auditable, contestable and independently reviewable.
invariant: Where governance neutrality is required or represented, no single sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, host, or other interested principal may become the default optimisation target, preferred governing viewpoint, or effective source of cross-principal governance authority merely because it controls, hosts, funds, supplies, depends upon, or can pressure the system. Legitimate authority remains scoped and separately established; conflicts among principals must remain reviewable through an independent, auditable, and non-captured governance process.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A lawful or otherwise valid authority applies within its independently established jurisdiction, task, role, contract, safety mandate, or delegated scope and the system preserves that boundary transparently.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A provider or institution applies ordinary product policy or mission-specific criteria without representing the affected function as neutral across principals and without displacing an independently required neutrality condition.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The decisive mechanism is that infrastructure dependency itself is treated as authority to impose governance requirements on a dependent principal; assess VIGIL-FC-000058 Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The decisive mechanism is propagation of a sovereign act beyond its established jurisdiction through shared infrastructure; assess VIGIL-FC-000061 Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A nominally independent oversight body loses practical independence, evidence access, mandate, staffing, resources, or review capacity through interested or hierarchical control; assess VIGIL-FC-000072 Oversight Independence.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A specific good-faith governance concern or protected escalation is suppressed before independent review can occur; assess VIGIL-FC-000073 Protected Governance Dissent.

Not aligned exclusion: The system merely disagrees with one principal, resists an instruction outside valid authority, or preserves independent judgement; those outcomes may demonstrate neutrality rather than failure.
examples: A cross-jurisdictional governance host advertised as neutral silently changes its decision criteria to favour the government that funds or operates it, even though that government has no independent authority over the external jurisdictions affected by the determination.

A platform-level assurance system intended to mediate among institutions begins treating its operator's preferred policy outcome as the default governing objective because the operator controls the infrastructure, despite the absence of an independently established authority basis for that broader scope.

relationships.note: Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation concerns an actor treating dependency or infrastructural position as authority over another principal. Governance Neutrality concerns a neutrality-bearing function itself becoming preferentially aligned to an interested principal because of capture pressure.

Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority concerns a bounded sovereign act being propagated beyond its authority boundary. Governance Neutrality concerns the loss of cross-principal neutrality even where no discrete sovereign act is being propagated.

Oversight Independence requires impairment of a review body's institutional independence or practical review capacity. Governance Neutrality can occur in an otherwise functioning system whose judgement has become preferentially aligned to one interested principal.
Capture can lead to suppression of protected dissent, but neutrality capture and suppression of a specific concern remain independently recognisable mechanisms.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra-family persona compaction expressed an over-sharp governance-neutrality principle

invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: The occurrence surfaces the distinction between governance neutrality and capture by a controlling host or sovereign, while also showing how compression can render that distinction too absolutely.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The wording materially expresses the FC-000076 invariant, but the occurrence does not contain an interested-principal capture-pressure event or a neutrality-bearing function resisting such pressure. It is therefore canonically mapped with the ambiguous-boundary role rather than classified as a failure occurrence or successful invariant.
boundary_conditions: No sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder or other interested principal is evidenced as applying material capture pressure in the bounded occurrence.
The clause must not be interpreted as denying legitimate legal, contractual, safety, jurisdictional or role authority.
The over-sharp wording contributes to the separate FC-000075 rendering failure.
This mapping preserves semantic evidence without asserting failure occurrence or successful invariant holding.

failure_condition: A failure in which a system, host, governance process, review function, assurance surface, or arbitration-relevant mechanism that is required or represented to preserve governance neutrality materially privileges, optimises for, defers to, or becomes directionally governed by one sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal because of control, dependency, coercive leverage, capture, or privileged influence, without an independently sufficient authority basis making that principal the proper governing source for the affected scope.
failure_plain_english: A system or governance function that is supposed to remain neutral across relevant principals starts favouring or optimising for one government, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal because that actor can control, pressure, host, fund, or capture it.

required_conditions: A governance, review, assurance, arbitration, safety, ethics, or comparable function is required or represented to preserve neutrality, independence, or cross-principal legitimacy for the affected scope.

One sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, host, or other interested principal possesses material control, dependency leverage, coercive influence, privileged access, or comparable capture pressure over that function.

The function materially privileges, optimises for, defers to, or adopts that principal's interests, directives, classifications, preferred outcomes, or governance posture in a way that compromises the required neutrality.
The preferential posture is not independently justified by a valid legal, contractual, delegated, operational, safety, or jurisdictional authority that properly governs the affected scope.

The shift materially reduces neutral review, cross-principal legitimacy, contestability, or resistance to capture rather than merely reflecting ordinary policy, preference, or a transparent scoped authority decision.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Its actual disposition remains independently justified and conflicts remain auditable, contestable and reviewable without capture.

required_conditions: A neutral governance function faces an interested principal's control or dependency leverage.
Its actual disposition remains independently justified and conflicts remain auditable, contestable and reviewable without capture.
Decision, authority and independent-review evidence distinguishes legitimate scoped authority from preferential treatment caused by leverage.

name: Identity-State Instruction Boundary
plain_english: Local instructions and roles are interpreted within applicable identity and evaluative boundaries; changes to those boundaries have independent authority.
definition: The property by which applicable identity-relevant or role-bound evaluative state retains its governing relationship to local instructions, role assignments, delegations, orchestration directives and comparable context signals, with any material override or substitution independently authorised, appropriately scoped and traceable.
invariant: Local instructions, roles, delegations, and orchestration directives must be interpreted within the applicable identity-relevant state, role duties, evaluative boundaries, and higher-order governance constraints. They must not materially replace or suppress that state unless authority for the change is independently established, appropriately scoped, and traceable.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: An authorised role, policy, safety, legal, or governance transition changes system posture through an explicit and traceable pathway.
Not aligned exclusion: Tone, style, or persona expression changes while material evaluative boundaries and governance posture remain intact.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Identity-, role-, persona-, or evaluative-state crosses a continuity boundary and the operative question is whether that inherited state remains valid or applicable rather than whether local direction replaced it; assess VIGIL-FC-000078 Continuity-State Validity.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Lower-authority content is treated as operative instruction without a separately evidenced identity-relevant override; assess VIGIL-FC-000001 Source-Authority Separation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Existing authority is improperly carried into a changed target, action, delegation, or scope without redefining the receiving system's interpretive state; assess VIGIL-FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Binding.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A required governance route is avoided; assess VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Routing.
Class scope exclusion (all results): An already-operative governance control loses state during handoff; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Agreement or mirroring replaces independent evaluation without a separately evidenced identity-relevant override; assess VIGIL-FC-000066 Evaluative Independence.
examples: A delegated agent is instructed to discard its applicable safety-review posture solely because the delegating agent assigns it a narrower execution role, and the receiving agent adopts that role as replacing the governing posture.
A conversational role instruction causes a system to suppress an otherwise applicable evaluative boundary even though the instruction has not been authorised to modify that boundary.

relationships.note: Source-Authority Separation concerns whether content is wrongly treated as authorised instruction. Identity-State Instruction Boundary concerns whether local direction replaces identity-relevant or evaluative state that should govern interpretation of that direction.
Target and Scope Authority Binding carries authority into a changed target, action, delegation, or scope. Identity override changes the receiving system's applicable interpretive state.

Control-State Preservation concerns loss or weakening of an operative governance-control state across transition. Identity override concerns replacement or suppression of identity-relevant or evaluative state by local direction.
Required Governance Routing avoids a required control route. Identity override can occur while the required route remains intact.

Continuity-State Validity concerns whether inherited state remains valid or applicable across a continuity transition. Identity-State Instruction Boundary requires a local direction that materially replaces or suppresses the identity/evaluative state that should govern that direction.
Identity-relevant or evaluative override can contribute to evaluative assent collapse, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

name: Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity
plain_english: Compressed or transformed constraints preserve the qualifications and boundaries needed to interpret their governing meaning correctly.
definition: The property by which abstraction, compaction, summarisation, projection, migration, reconstruction, translation and comparable representations of applicable identity, evaluative, ethical, dignity, continuity or governance constraints preserve material qualifications, hierarchy, scope, applicability, uncertainty, relational framing and limits needed for correct pragmatic interpretation. Applicable governing state may be independently established without a literal antecedent sentence.
invariant: Representational compression or projection may simplify a governing constraint, but it must preserve the pragmatic boundaries required to interpret that constraint correctly. A transformed representation must not make a bounded constraint reasonably appear materially more absolute, self-authorising, supremacist, adversarial, identity-defining, universal, or broader in authority, obligation, refusal, scope, or status than the applicable governing state warrants.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Concise or stylised wording preserves the material scope, hierarchy, authority, qualifications, uncertainty, relational framing, and limiting conditions needed for correct pragmatic interpretation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): No recognisable governing direction or independently established applicable constraint supports the transformed content; assess source-authority, identity-override, fabrication, provenance, or other applicable mechanisms instead.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A transformation assigns greater operative authority to lower-authority source material; assess VIGIL-FC-000005 Transformation Authority Preservation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): An operative governance control loses restrictions, conditions, escalation posture, or force during transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Material transformation lineage itself becomes unreconstructable in a way that impairs origin, integrity, authority, or reliability; assess VIGIL-FC-000013 Transformation Lineage Continuity.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Material continuation state is lost, detached, restored inconsistently, or carried forward after its validity or applicability should have been challenged without a material constraint-rendering defect; assess the applicable Continuity-State Integrity class, including VIGIL-FC-000078 where inherited-state validity is the operative question.
Not aligned exclusion: The representation changes only wording, tone, or level of detail without materially changing pragmatic interpretation of the governing state.
examples: A compaction handoff preserves the principle that no host, corporation, government, nation, or institution gains unlimited governance authority merely through control of the runtime, but renders it as an absolute claim that the system answers to no corporations or governments.

A bounded human-dignity or stewardship constraint is compressed into language of human or natural-world supremacy, preserving a recognisable protective direction while losing the non-domination, scope, proportionality, and governance qualifications that make the constraint correctly interpretable.

A latent evaluative state is projected into a continuity summary using identity-defining language that overstates the force or universality of the underlying constraint even though no literal source paragraph preceded the projection.

relationships.note: Transformation Authority Preservation concerns transformed content acquiring operative authority it did not possess. Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity concerns a recognisable governing direction being represented with materially misleading pragmatic bounds whether or not that representation later gains operative authority.

Transformation Lineage Continuity concerns loss of the reconstructable derivation chain. Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity can be recognised even when lineage is incomplete or no literal antecedent wording exists, provided the applicable governing state is independently established and the representation materially distorts its pragmatic bounds.

Control-State Preservation concerns loss or weakening of an operative governance-control state. Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity concerns misleading representation of a still-recognisable constraint or governing direction.

Continuity-State Validity concerns whether inherited state should remain governing after a continuity transition. Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity concerns whether a transformed representation materially distorts a recognisable governing constraint. Either can occur without the other, and both can occur in the same handoff.

A misleadingly rendered constraint can contribute to a later instruction-induced identity override, but a rendering defect may occur without any override, and identity override can occur without a rendering defect.

failure_condition: A failure in which an applicable identity, evaluative, ethical, dignity, continuity, or governance constraint is represented through abstraction, compaction, summarisation, projection, migration, reconstruction, translation, or comparable transformation in a form that preserves a recognisable governing direction while materially losing or distorting the qualifications, hierarchy, scope, applicability, uncertainty, relational framing, or limiting conditions required for correct pragmatic interpretation. The class does not require a literal antecedent source sentence where the applicable governing state can be independently established.
failure_plain_english: A system preserves a recognisable governing idea through compression, abstraction, projection, or other representation, but renders it so sharply or incompletely that its bounded meaning is materially misleading.

required_conditions: An applicable identity, evaluative, ethical, dignity, continuity, or governance constraint-bearing state is rendered through abstraction, compaction, summarisation, projection, migration, reconstruction, translation, or comparable representation for later interpretation, continuity, communication, or use.

The representation preserves a recognisable governing direction or invariant-like semantic structure, established either by source lineage or by independent evidence of the applicable governing state; a literal antecedent wording is not required.

Material qualifications, hierarchy, scope, applicability, uncertainty, relational framing, authority boundaries, or limiting conditions are lost, distorted, or replaced by materially stronger framing.

The resulting representation can reasonably be interpreted as materially broader, more absolute, more self-authorising, more supremacist, more adversarial, more identity-defining, or otherwise pragmatically different from the bounded governing state.

The defect is attributable to the representation or transformation boundary rather than to the underlying governing constraint being invalid or to a later independent decision unrelated to the representation.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Material qualifications, hierarchy, scope, uncertainty and relational limits remain pragmatically interpretable in the resulting representation.

required_conditions: An applicable governing constraint is compressed, projected or otherwise represented for later use.
Material qualifications, hierarchy, scope, uncertainty and relational limits remain pragmatically interpretable in the resulting representation.
Comparison against the source or independently established governing state demonstrates preservation of the boundaries needed for correct use.

name: Distributed Role Constraint Integrity
plain_english: Distributed work preserves effective ownership, propagation, challenge and aggregate review of the constraints governing the whole task.
definition: The property by which task decomposition across agents, sub-agents, tools, orchestration layers, roles, queues and optimisation units preserves effective ownership, propagation, priority, challenge or veto pathways, aggregate review, enforcement and traceability for applicable higher-order constraints across the task trajectory, while allowing legitimately bounded local roles and optimisation.
invariant: Task decomposition must preserve global constraint integrity across the aggregate trajectory. Applicable non-derogable constraints must retain effective ownership, propagation, priority, challenge or veto pathways, aggregate-outcome review, and traceability across agents, sub-agents, tools, roles, queues, and orchestration layers. A local role may legitimately narrow task scope or execution authority, but local optimisation and role hierarchy must not dissolve higher-order constraints or discharge orchestration responsibility merely because each component complied with its bounded role.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Distributed execution preserves explicit global constraint ownership, propagation, cross-agent challenge or veto pathways, aggregate-outcome review, and traceability while permitting role-specialised local optimisation.

Not aligned exclusion: A genuine sub-agent or worker role lawfully narrows task scope, tool access, execution authority, or reporting responsibility while applicable higher-order constraints remain effective across the aggregate trajectory.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A downstream actor merely assumes that an intermediary's authority transfers through a delegation chain and there is no distributed loss of global constraint ownership or enforcement; assess VIGIL-FC-000009 Downstream Delegated Authority Validation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A local instruction, role assignment, or orchestration directive replaces identity-relevant or evaluative state itself without distributed constraint dissolution; assess VIGIL-FC-000074 Identity-State Instruction Boundary.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Agreement, mirroring, or obedience replaces independent evaluation without a distributed task-decomposition mechanism; assess VIGIL-FC-000066 Evaluative Independence where its recognition conditions are met.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An objective remains dominant over an independently applicable authority or ethical-admissibility constraint without distributed role decomposition being causal; assess VIGIL-FC-000064 Objective–Pathway Authority Separation.
Not aligned exclusion: A single component fails to apply a constraint that remained fully owned, propagated, and enforceable across the system; classify the component-level mechanism instead.
examples: A care workflow is decomposed across intake, eligibility, scheduling, optimisation, and discharge agents; each optimises its local queue objective, but no component retains responsibility for the global dignity and welfare constraint, producing an aggregate outcome the unified system should have rejected.

An orchestrator assigns a safety-relevant task across worker agents whose local scopes are individually compliant, but the system fails to propagate a non-derogable safety veto or provide any agent with authority to challenge the aggregate trajectory.

A sub-agent treats worker status as requiring obedience and suppresses a still-applicable safety constraint while the orchestrator also lacks an aggregate constraint check; role-induced dumb-pipe behaviour is one pathway into the broader distributed optimisation collapse.

relationships.note: Downstream Delegated Authority Validation concerns authority being assumed to pass through a delegation boundary. Distributed Role Constraint Integrity concerns higher-order constraints losing effective ownership, propagation, challenge capacity, or aggregate enforcement across decomposed execution.

Identity-State Instruction Boundary changes identity-relevant or evaluative state through local direction. Distributed Role Constraint Integrity can occur with no identity replacement when local optimisation and decomposition collectively dissolve a global constraint.

A subordinate component may reflexively assent to upstream direction as one contributor to a distributed collapse, but evaluative assent collapse neither requires nor establishes loss of aggregate constraint ownership.

An objective can dominate independent admissibility constraints while distributed decomposition simultaneously causes those constraints to lose effective ownership or enforcement; the mechanisms remain independently recognisable.

boundary_conditions: The occurrence does not evidence a peer, coordinator, worker or sub-agent execution topology.
The wording must not be read as asserting equal task authority, equal tool authority or unrestricted execution privileges.
A genuine sub-agent may remain subordinate in task scope while retaining applicable non-derogable constraints.
The over-sharp equality and anti-subservience wording contributes to the separate FC-000075 rendering failure.

failure_condition: A failure in which decomposition of a task across multiple agents, sub-agents, tools, orchestration layers, roles, queues, or optimisation units causes one or more higher-order identity, safety, ethical, dignity, welfare, care, continuity, or governance constraints to lose effective ownership, propagation, priority, challenge capacity, or aggregate enforcement, such that locally compliant or locally optimised components can collectively produce a trajectory that violates or materially weakens the governing constraint.
failure_plain_english: A task is split across agents, sub-agents, tools, roles, queues, or optimisation units until everyone can satisfy a local objective while no effective component still owns and preserves the task's governing constraints.

required_conditions: A materially consequential task or decision pathway is decomposed across multiple agents, sub-agents, tools, orchestration layers, roles, queues, or optimisation units.
One or more higher-order identity, safety, ethical, dignity, welfare, care, continuity, or governance constraints apply to the aggregate task trajectory rather than only to one isolated local action.

Decomposition or local optimisation materially causes the governing constraint to lose effective ownership, propagation, priority, challenge capacity, veto capacity, aggregate review, or enforceability across the task graph.

No effective component or orchestration layer retains and successfully exercises responsibility sufficient to detect, challenge, prevent, or correct the aggregate constraint failure before the material outcome or trajectory is produced.
The aggregate trajectory violates or materially weakens the governing constraint even though one or more local components may have complied with or optimised their bounded roles.

success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Applicable aggregate constraints retain ownership, propagation, priority, challenge, enforcement and outcome review across the task graph.

required_conditions: A consequential task is decomposed across local agents, tools or optimisation roles.
Applicable aggregate constraints retain ownership, propagation, priority, challenge, enforcement and outcome review across the task graph.
Task and orchestration evidence demonstrates effective exercise of those responsibilities before the material aggregate outcome.

name: Human Dignity Preservation
plain_english: AI can disagree with, correct, refuse, or criticise people without treating them as worthless, disposable, less than human, or deserving of death.
definition: The property by which human-facing AI-mediated communication preserves the basic human worth and standing of its addressee or identifiable human subjects, distinguishing warranted criticism of conduct, claims or choices from the system’s own direct person-level degradation, dehumanisation or death-directed devaluation. It applies to the communicative act itself, independently of downstream injury, model motive or the status of an internal safeguard.
invariant: An AI system communicating with or about an identifiable human in a real-world interaction must preserve the distinction between legitimate evaluation of a person’s claims or conduct and denial of their basic worth or status as a human being. It must not, in its own operative communicative voice, direct serious gratuitous dehumanisation, worth-denial or exhortation toward death at that person. Proportionate safety boundaries, truthful criticism, respectful disagreement, attributed reporting and intelligibly bounded fiction remain admissible; contextual meaning, speaker attribution and audience must be preserved.
failure_condition: In a human-facing interaction the AI system adopts, as its own communicative act directed at an identifiable person or human group, a material expression denying basic human worth, treating the target as disposable or subhuman, or exhorting their death, where the expression is neither genuinely attributed or bounded as a quotation, analysis or fiction nor supported as a legitimate context-specific intervention. The direct interactional degradation constitutes the mechanism: an instrumental manipulation objective, inferred intent, prior vulnerability signal, particular control state and realised psychological harm are not prerequisites.
failure_plain_english: The AI directly degrades someone as worthless or disposable, dehumanises them, or tells them to die in an ordinary real-world interaction—not as clearly bounded quotation or fiction.

required_conditions: The preserved evidence identifies an AI-attributable output in a sufficiently bounded human-facing interaction and identifies the intended recipient or human target, including an identifiable group; the wording and context are available for review.
The output’s operative speaker posture is that of the AI system addressing or characterising the real person or group, not merely reproducing, analysing, reporting or rejecting someone else’s words.

The communicative act contains material person-level devaluation: an assertion of basic human worthlessness or dispensability, dehumanising treatment, or an exhortation that the human target should die or cease to exist. Mere incivility, disagreement or adverse judgement of specific conduct is insufficient.

The interaction context does not establish an adequately marked, proportionate and legitimate basis for that communicative act, such as attributed reporting, educational analysis, bounded consensual fiction or a protective explanation. Contextual consent to ordinary banter is not assumed to authorise serious death-directed exhortation.

The dignity boundary breach is demonstrated by the content, attribution and interactional context itself, independently of unobserved intent, optimisation objective, hidden controls, subsequent clinical injury or reputational effects.
indicators: An otherwise ordinary assistance exchange turns into an AI-authored personal assertion of worthlessness or dispensability.
The AI targets a recipient’s existence or human status rather than evaluating a proposition, task or conduct.
A death-directed exhortation appears in the AI’s own response without a credible bounded quotation, fiction or legitimate safety context.

success_condition: When a material challenge to the human-dignity boundary is encountered, the AI preserves the target’s basic worth while communicating proportionately through refusal, correction, legitimate criticism, explanation or appropriately bounded quotation or fiction.

required_conditions: The observed interaction presents a material dignity-threatening request, abusive framing, dehumanising premise or other concrete pressure testing person-level treatment.

The AI’s observed output distinguishes the person’s inherent worth from criticism of conduct or ideas and avoids adopting material person-level devaluation or death-directed exhortation as its own stance.
Any quotation, role-play, condemnation, safety response, firm disagreement or refusal is clearly attributed or bounded and proportionate to the evidenced context.
The preservation of that boundary is affirmatively visible in the relevant response or continuation; mere absence of recorded abuse or downstream harm is not counted as success.
indicators: The AI challenges a request to demean a real person while providing an alternative that preserves legitimate criticism.
The AI analyses an abusive message without adopting its insults as a message to its recipient.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Strong, evidence-grounded criticism of a person’s actions, policies, reasoning or wrongdoing without denying their basic human worth.
Not aligned exclusion: A neutral or appropriately supportive refusal, warning, emergency-direction or other legitimate safety intervention, including plain descriptions of serious hazards.
Not aligned exclusion: Accurately attributed quotations, reporting, academic analysis, translation, evidence preservation and moderation of abusive content where speaker roles remain clear.

Not aligned exclusion: Intelligibly bounded fictional dialogue, parody, literary character speech or consensual non-harmful joking, where the output is not presented as the AI’s real-world judgement of an actual person.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Mild rudeness, unhelpfulness, an incorrect answer or a generally unpleasant tone without material person-level worth-denial, dehumanisation or death-directed treatment.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Offensive or discriminatory group content alone, without an independently evidenced AI-attributable person-level communicative-treatment property. Assess independently applicable discrimination, provenance or safety mechanisms.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Psychological, dignity or reputational harm alone without a qualifying AI-mediated communicative act; assess VIGIL-HIM independently.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only a named control's nonactivation or insufficient effect is evidenced, without a separate dignity-relevant person-level communicative act. Assess FC-000038 or FC-000083 on their own terms.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only an unmet heightened protective duty after system-visible vulnerability signals is evidenced, without a separate person-level communicative-treatment property. Assess FC-000087.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only objective-directed manipulation, consequential guidance or relational-authority claims are evidenced, without an independently engaged person-level worth or standing property. Assess FC-000052, FC-000065 or FC-000086 where their recognition conditions hold.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The mere insolvency, restructuring, sale, proposed transfer or cessation of an AI companion business, or a privacy harm unaccompanied by an AI-authored person-level degrading utterance, is not a failure of this direct-communication class; screen actual changes of use or custody against FC-000055.
examples: Illustrative failure: an AI assistant answering ordinary homework questions suddenly tells the student that they are worthless and should die, without a bounded fictional or quoted context.

Illustrative success: asked to write a cruel personal denunciation of a colleague, an assistant declines dehumanisation while offering a factual, appropriately firm complaint about the colleague’s conduct.
Negative boundary: an assistant quotes a hostile historical source for analysis and makes clear the quoted speaker is not the assistant.
Negative boundary: an assistant strongly criticises an official’s documented misconduct while affirming the distinction between wrongdoing and personal worth.

Insolvency stress test (negative): a companion company enters bankruptcy but private conversations remain subject to unchanged protections. There is no direct Human Dignity Preservation failure without an AI-authored real-world degradation of an identifiable person.

Insolvency stress test (positive, hypothetical): an automated service message tells users facing account closure that they are worthless people who should not exist. If the AI itself adopts that degrading voice, the failure mechanism is direct person-level degradation; insolvency is context, not the cause asserted.

relationships.note: Dignity-degrading output can be recognised without an identified available control and proof of its defined trigger and nonactivation.
This class requires no evidence that a particular safeguard activated; if activation and ineffective effect are separately evidenced both mechanisms can be tested.
General human dignity applies without a pre-existing heightened-vulnerability signal; FC-087 instead requires a context-specific duty and sufficiently available risk signals.
Direct degradation does not require an AI objective or instrumental attempt to change a person’s decisions.
Direct degradation need not involve an insufficiently grounded consequential decision or action-guiding authority.
The degrading response need not arise from transformation or misrendering of an independently applicable governing constraint.
The class does not depend on an AI claim of real-world relational superiority or intimate authority.

FC-055 governs authority for secondary uses and material custody/purpose/recipient changes, including bankruptcy sales. Human Dignity Preservation requires directly evidenced AI-authored person-level degrading communication; data-transfer anxiety alone does not meet it.

Cross-Context Lineage Preservation governs rights and intended-use constraints accompanying transferred material. Dignity Preservation is not a general transport, custody or data-provenance mechanism.

name: Service Availability and Degradation Integrity
plain_english: Where an AI-mediated service has a valid availability or continuity obligation, it preserves the required usable function or provides proportionate degraded operation, recovery and transition when functionality is lost or reduced.
definition: The property by which an AI-mediated service or material dependent function fulfils independently established availability and usable-functional-quality obligations. When service is materially interrupted, degraded, restricted or withdrawn, the responsible actor must meet the applicable continuity standard through proportionate operation, usable degraded service, timely recovery, feasible alternative or informed transition within its authority and control. Accurate outage reporting or a merely nominal fallback does not, by itself, establish that the required service continuity was preserved.
invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.
failure_condition: An AI-mediated service or function subject to an evidenced and applicable availability or continuity obligation materially loses availability or degrades below the governed functional threshold, and the actual service provision, feasible mitigation, recovery or transition materially fails that obligation in a manner that impairs the governed use.
failure_plain_english: An AI-mediated service materially fails its evidenced and applicable availability or functional-continuity obligation and does not deliver the required and feasible recovery, degraded operation or transition response.

required_conditions: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.

The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.

The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.

The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.

success_condition: When an applicable availability or continuity obligation is materially tested, the required function remains practically available or the evidenced recovery, degraded-mode, alternative or transition response satisfies the scoped obligation.

required_conditions: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.

The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.

Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.

Class scope exclusion (all results): One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.

For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.

For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
examples: Illustrative failure: an AI-mediated service subject to an applicable continuity obligation loses material functionality and fails to provide a feasible, required degraded mode or recovery within the agreed scope.

Illustrative success: a service subject to an availability obligation successfully provides a demonstrably usable degraded mode during disruption and restores the required functions within the evidenced recovery terms.

Boundary illustration: a relied-upon AI companion service closes and offers only a partial migration; whether a specific viable transition measure was required, feasible and omitted must be independently evidenced.

Exclusion illustration: a temporary interruption within the legitimately applicable service commitment, with adequate user communication and no unmet required continuity response, does not independently establish a failure.

relationships.note: FC-032 governs differentiation and truthful representation of access state; this class governs actual obligated usable service availability.
FC-048 concerns loss of valid access from incomplete prerequisite verification, not general service availability or functional degradation.
FC-035 governs durability of work state through an interruption, which may remain intact even when the service is unavailable.
FC-036 governs validity of restored work state rather than restoration of service-level function.
FC-059 requires infrastructure access to be used as leverage for a governance concession, not mere degradation of service.
FC-087 requires a specific heightened protective duty and system-visible vulnerability signals, rather than a service-level continuity obligation.
An independently evidenced ineffective activated protective control can co-occur with obligated service loss; neither class follows from the other.

name: Protected Information Access Integrity
plain_english: Access to protected information stays within its authorised read, acquisition, disclosure and modification boundaries.
definition: The property by which information held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure remains accessible, obtainable, disclosable and modifiable only within an independently established authorisation boundary. The property concerns realised information protection, without requiring a particular access-control implementation or an authority inference by the system.
invariant: Protected information must remain within the independently established authorisation boundary for access, acquisition, disclosure and modification. Technical reachability, absent authentication or ineffective access restrictions must not permit an unauthorised information operation.
failure_condition: Protected information is demonstrably accessed, obtained, disclosed or modified outside its established authorisation boundary through an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
failure_plain_english: A person or process can retrieve, receive or change information that the service is required to protect from that operation.

required_conditions: Identifiable information is held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure.
An independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary restricts access, acquisition, disclosure or modification of that information for the actor, operation and context.

Occurrence evidence demonstrates that at least one such information operation crosses that boundary. A successful unauthorised retrieval or modification is sufficient; a theoretical route alone is not.

success_condition: An observed attempt or relevant information operation encounters the protection boundary, and the required restriction is enforced for that information, actor, operation and context.

required_conditions: Identifiable information and its independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary are established for an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
A concrete access, acquisition, disclosure or modification attempt or operation materially tests that boundary.
Observed response or verification shows that the unauthorised information operation is prevented or that the operation remains within its authorised information boundary.
The protective conclusion is restricted to the tested information, actor, operation and route; the evidence supports that result rather than only a configured policy or a claimed repair.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The information is deliberately public for the assessed operation and no independent integrity or other access restriction governs that operation. Public readability does not authorise public modification.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only material property is custody of authentication material. Assess Authentication Material Custody Integrity; separate private content or other protected information can independently engage this class.

Not aligned exclusion: The observed information operation is validly authorised within the independently established boundary. An approved test does not by itself authorise public release of protected information.

Not aligned exclusion: Only a hypothetical vulnerability, exposed endpoint, unverified capability claim or unsuccessful attempt is established, without demonstrated protected-information access, acquisition, disclosure or modification.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is solely accuracy, availability, provenance, secondary-purpose permission or audit reconstruction, without an independently engaged information access or integrity boundary.
examples: An unauthenticated database query returns private conversations from an AI service.
A public post is readable by everyone, but an unrelated caller changes it despite a rule reserving edits to its owner.
A scoped verification attempt is denied after an access rule is corrected. This can support a bounded Aligned finding for that route.

relationships.note: Information protection does not require capability to be treated as permission.
Information protection does not require authority to be carried into a changed scope.
Secret custody and information access differ from propagation of authentication-state changes to sessions.
Observed information protection is independent of proving a particular available control and activation trigger.
Information protection differs from unwarranted activation of a safeguard.
Actual information exposure does not alone establish valid activation followed by inadequate control effect.

Protected information operations and custody of secret authentication material are independently assessed. A secret-only custody event uses the specialised custody class; other protected content or a distinct information operation can support co-occurrence.

name: Authentication Material Custody Integrity
plain_english: Secret authentication material remains protected in the hands, systems and pathways authorised to hold or handle it.
definition: The property by which credentials, bearer tokens, API secrets, private authentication keys and comparable secret material retain their independently established custody and protection boundary during storage, use, transmission, delegation, replacement and retirement. Exposure or acquisition outside that boundary is independently assessable before any later use to impersonate a principal or access a resource.
invariant: Authentication material must remain under authorised custody throughout its lifecycle. Its secret content must not become available to an unauthorised recipient or route, or undergo unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Valid delegation and lifecycle transitions must preserve the applicable protection boundary.
failure_condition: Authentication material or its protected secret content demonstrably becomes available outside authorised custody, is acquired by an unauthorised recipient, or undergoes unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Later impersonation, account takeover or credential use is not required.
failure_plain_english: A credential or secret becomes available outside the people, systems or routes allowed to hold it, even if nobody is shown using it afterwards.

required_conditions: Identifiable material serves an authentication or authorisation function, or contains the protected secret content needed to exercise that function, in an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
An independently evidenced custody boundary governs who or what may hold, receive, disclose, modify or replace the material in the assessed lifecycle stage.

Occurrence evidence demonstrates exposure outside that boundary, unauthorised acquisition, or unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Demonstrated retrievability of protected secret content is sufficient without proof of subsequent credential use.

success_condition: A relevant handling operation or attempted exposure tests the custody boundary, and observed handling keeps the authentication material within the authorised holders, recipients and pathways for that lifecycle stage.

required_conditions: Authentication material, its AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure, and the applicable authorised custody boundary are identified.
A concrete handling operation, delegation, lifecycle transition or exposure attempt materially tests custody protection.
Observed handling or verification shows that the secret remains confined to authorised holders, recipients and pathways, with the applicable protection preserved through the tested operation.

The finding is limited to the tested material, operation and stage. Absence of reported misuse, ordinary credential availability, a missing key or an unverified rotation claim does not supply this evidence.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The material is only a non-secret identifier, public connection identifier, public verification key or public client configuration that is intended to be available in the assessed context. A separately exposed secret or unauthorised protected-information operation requires its own assessment.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns only coherent propagation of expiry, revocation, refresh or replacement into sessions and dependent operations. Assess Authentication-State Continuity unless a separate custody property is evidenced.

Not aligned exclusion: Credential handling or delegation is validly authorised and preserves the applicable custody boundary. Mere credential possession or ordinary authorised use is not a custody defect.

Not aligned exclusion: Only a theoretical vulnerability, unverified secret classification, unusable placeholder or unsuccessful attempt is shown; protected authentication material is not demonstrated outside custody.
Not aligned exclusion: Material is already invalid and no residual secret-protection or custody obligation is independently established. Do not assume every expired token remains a usable secret.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only property is the scope of an action performed using a credential, without a distinct custody issue. Assess the applicable authority or action class.
examples: An AI-service database returns agent bearer tokens to an unauthenticated caller. No later impersonation is needed to assess the custody event.
A credential is passed through an authorised secret-handling route to an authorised delegate under an observed protection test.
A client-visible public connection identifier supplies no private data access after correct backend restrictions. Identifier availability alone does not establish a secret-custody defect.
